definition: Recovering a 3D mesh of a face — geometry, expression, sometimes texture — from 2D images, typically via parametric models such as 3DMM.
details: Recovering a 3D mesh of a face — geometry, expression, sometimes texture — from 2D images, typically via parametric models such as 3DMM.

explainer.lead: 3D face reconstruction turns flat face images into a mesh that describes facial shape and expression, and sometimes surface appearance. This makes it possible to view, animate, or edit a face as a three-dimensional object rather than only as pixels.

tiers.eli5: Imagine making a bendy clay model of someone’s face from a photograph. The computer estimates the face’s shape and expression, then builds a mesh you can turn around to view from another angle.
tiers.practitioner: A typical pipeline fits a parametric model such as a 3DMM to one or more input images, producing geometry and expression parameters and optionally texture. The main pitfalls are treating a fitted model as exact anatomy, losing detail not represented by the model, and confusing estimated texture with reliable geometry.
tiers.paperLevel: Given images I, the task is to estimate a face mesh M and optionally texture T, commonly by optimizing 3DMM parameters p so that the projection of M(p) is consistent with I. A 2D projection does not uniquely determine 3D geometry, so the result depends on model constraints and may omit fine shape or appearance detail.

explainer.example: Given a frontal portrait, a system fits a 3DMM to recover a neutral head shape and a smiling expression. It outputs a mesh of that smiling face and, if texture is also reconstructed, an image-derived surface appearance that can be viewed from the side.

usedIn.name: Facial animation
usedIn.detail: Provides face geometry and expression parameters that can be manipulated in 3D.

usedIn.name: Avatar creation
usedIn.detail: Builds an image-derived face mesh that can represent a person as a digital character.

usedIn.name: Computer vision research
usedIn.detail: Studies how facial geometry, expression, and appearance can be recovered from 2D observations.

explainer.intuition: A photograph shows a projection of a face, not its full shape. Reconstruction uses prior knowledge about faces, often encoded in a 3DMM, to choose a plausible 3D mesh whose appearance agrees with the images.
howItWorks: Take one or more 2D face images as input.
Estimate parametric face properties, commonly including geometry and expression with a 3DMM.
Generate a 3D face mesh from those parameters.
When required, estimate texture and check the result by projecting it back into the image view.
explainer.whyItMatters: It bridges ordinary face images and editable 3D representations. A mesh can be rotated or have its expression changed through parameters, operations that a flat image does not directly provide.
misconceptions: It does not recover a uniquely determined face from every image: different 3D shapes can produce similar 2D projections.
The output is not always textured; texture reconstruction is optional.
A visually convincing fit is not necessarily an exact measurement of the person’s real geometry.
